extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, appellants, patent practitioners, and Administrative Patent Judges (APJs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on procedures and substantive requirements after a Board decision on an ex parte appeal, including new grounds of rejection, rehearing, publication, and examiner actions following Board decisions. Targets USPTO/Board practice for examiners and appellants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board suspension of appeal pending court action
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may refuse to consider an appeal until after conclusion of a pending civil action or appeal to the Federal Circuit when issues are identical or similar and a court decision may be determinative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension is recognized as sound practice to permit the Board to benefit from a court decision; an appellant may not use prolonged pendency of court proceedings to avoid res judicata and relitigate essentially the same issue in another application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to withhold decision to permit refiling
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant may petition that the Board’s decision be withheld to permit refiling of the application at any time prior to mailing of the decision; up to 30 days may be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions filed early are more likely to be entertained (may obviate oral hearing or setting date). If case already set for oral hearing, petition should request vacatur of hearing date, not postponement. A withdrawal filed on the same day the decision is mailed will result in denial of a petition to vacate the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board remarks not authority to amend claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A remark by the Board that a certain feature does not appear in a claim is not to be taken as a statement that the claim may be allowed if the feature is supplied by amendment; such remark shall not be construed by appellant to give authority to amend the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellants should not treat Board comments as implicit permission to change claim scope; follow proper amendment procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of new ground of rejection (37 CFR 41.50(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board has knowledge of grounds not involved in the appeal for rejecting any pending claim, it may include a statement designating such as a new ground of rejection; such designation is not final for judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When such a non-final new ground is entered, the appellant has two months from the date of decision to (1) reopen prosecution by submitting an appropriate amendment and/or new evidence so the matter is remanded to the examiner, or (2) request rehearing under §41.52 addressing the new ground with particularity. The new ground is binding on the examiner unless overcome by amendment or new evidence not previously of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two response options to a new ground of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon a Board-designated new ground under 37 CFR 41.50(b), appellant must within two months either (1) reopen prosecution by appropriate amendment/new evidence (remand to examiner), or (2) request rehearing addressing the new ground and stating with particularity the points misapprehended or overlooked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely exercise one of these options will result in termination of the appeal as to the rejected claims. Arguments submitted without amendment/new evidence will be treated as a request for rehearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time extension limitations for 37 CFR 41.50 responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are not applicable to the time periods set forth for responses to Board decisions under this section; only 1.136(b) or 1.550(c) (for ex parte reexamination) may apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellants should not rely on routine 1.136(a) extensions to extend the two-month periods for reopening prosecution or requesting rehearing under 41.50(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and nature of appropriate amendment and new evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment is 'appropriate' if it amends one or more of the claims rejected or substitutes new claims to avoid the art or reasons adduced by the Board, and must be directed to the same subject matter as the appealed claims; 'new evidence' may be a showing under 37 CFR 1.130, 1.131 or 1.132 as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding new claims without amending or substituting for the rejected claims is not appropriate (new claims will not be entered and may be treated as a request for rehearing if they contain argument). Arguments submitted without amendment or new evidence will be treated as a rehearing request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited reopening of prosecution when new ground designated
rubrics_metrics.description: Reopening prosecution under 37 CFR 41.50(b)(1) reopens prosecution only as to the subject matter to which the new rejection was applied; affirmed rejections included in the Board decision remain non-open to further prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecution on the 41.50(b) rejection can incidentally overcome an affirmed rejection, but any subsequent appeal must be limited to the 41.50(b) rejection and may not include the affirmed rejection. If claims are allowed or application abandoned as a result of the limited prosecution, the application should not be returned to the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing requirements and limitations (37 CFR 41.52)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single request for rehearing may be filed within two months of the Board’s original decision; the request must state with particularity the points believed to have been misapprehended or overlooked by the Board. Arguments not raised in prior briefs and evidence not previously relied upon are not permitted except in limited circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted new arguments: (A) based on a recent relevant decision of the Board or Federal Court, (B) responding to a new ground of rejection designated under 41.50(b), and (C) that the Board's decision contains an undesignated new ground of rejection. Rehearing is on the written record — it does not entitle the appellant to another oral hearing as a matter of course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of rehearing (written record only)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'rehearing' means rehearing on the written record; it should not be interpreted as entitling an appellant to an oral hearing on the request for rehearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board does not normally grant rehearings as another oral hearing; rehearing proceedings are generally decided from the written submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public access to Board actions (37 CFR 41.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Board action is available for public inspection without a party’s permission if rendered in a file open to the public (37 CFR 1.11) or in an application published under 1.211–1.221. The Office may independently publish any Board action that is available for public inspection. The Director may also publish actions not otherwise publishable if special circumstances warrant and an affected party does not timely object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the Director intends to make such an action public, the party has two months to object in writing on trade secret/confidentiality grounds and identify deletions needed. The party gets at least twenty days to request reconsideration and seek court review before contested portions are made public over objection. Records of Board proceedings are available to the public unless the involved file is not open to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing triggers for appellate and rehearing periods
rubrics_metrics.description: The 63-day period for filing an appeal or commencing a civil action under 37 CFR 90.3 (or two-month period for rehearing under 37 CFR 41.52) begins to run from the 'mail date' if the decision is paper-delivered, or the 'notification date' if electronic, as shown on form PTOL-90A attached to the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must await expiration of the two-month rehearing period before taking further action if the Board decision affirms or affirms-in-part the examiner's decision. Proper determination of mail/notification date is critical to compute deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board retains jurisdiction until specific events after new ground designation
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Board designates a new ground under 41.50(b), the Board retains jurisdiction over the appeal until (a) the time for response expires and the Board enters an order of dismissal, or (b) the appellant reopens prosecution in response to the new grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant elects mixed responses (amend some claims, request rehearing on others), the examiner will not consider those claims for which rehearing is requested; rehearing will be considered after prosecution of the amended claims is terminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner actions following a complete reversal
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete reversal of the examiner's rejection brings the case up for immediate action by the examiner. If reversal does not place the application in condition for immediate allowance (e.g., Board entered new ground), examiner should follow guidance in MPEP §1214.06.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must not regard reversal as authority to make a new search to uncover other references; give full faith and credit to prior examiner's search. If examiner has specific knowledge of references indicating nonpatentability, submit to the Technology Center Director for authorization to reopen prosecution under 37 CFR 1.198. Examiner may request rehearing (normally within two months) — requests must be approved by TC Director and forwarded to Deputy Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy for approval before mailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner rehearing request content limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner's request for rehearing must state with particularity the points believed to have been misapprehended or overlooked by the Board. Arguments not raised in the answers before the Board and evidence not previously relied on are not permitted except that the examiner may present a new argument based on a recent relevant decision of the Board or a Federal Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for rehearing by examiners follow the same narrow scope rules as appellant rehearings and require supervisory and policy-office approvals before being served.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of withdrawn/not-appealed claims
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal is presumed taken from rejection of all claims (37 CFR 41.31(c)). Where appellant withdraws some appealed claims (e.g., did not present them for review in the brief), and the Board reverses on remaining appealed claims, the withdrawal is treated as authorization to cancel the withdrawn claims; examiner must notify appellant of cancellation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure withdrawn claims are properly cancelled and applicant/appellant is notified. See MPEP §1205.02 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures when examiner sustained in whole or in part (end of Board jurisdiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Board enters a final decision and time for judicial review has expired (or review sought), Board jurisdiction ends and examiner must take appropriate action depending on whether: (I) no claims stand allowed, (II) claims stand allowed, or (III) claims require action (e.g., reversal brings certain claims up on the merits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful handling required to avoid overlooking cases that leave Board jurisdiction. See subsections for concrete actions: abandonment, converting dependent claims to independent form, setting shortened statutory periods, issuing notices, issuing application or reexamination certificates, or returning files to Board if applicable. Follow specified form paragraphs (e.g., ¶12.291, ¶12.292, ¶12.297) and observe specified time limits and extension rules depending on scenario.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling when no claims stand allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: If no claims stand allowed after Board action, examiner should consider the application abandoned and may either convert dependent claims to independent form by examiner's amendment and issue application or set a one-month (or two-month in certain draft paragraph) time for applicant to rewrite dependent claim(s) in independent form; if no timely reply, application is abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph ¶12.291 (No Allowed Claim) may provide a TWO MONTH time period from mailing date to present dependent claims in independent form to avoid abandonment — extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are stated as available in that paragraph. Use correct paragraph and time period depending on whether notice of appeal was filed on/after Jan 23, 2012 and the case specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling when at least one claim stands allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: If at least one claim stands allowed, the examiner issues the application or reexamination certificate on allowed claims. If dependent claims are reversed to allowable only upon conversion to independent form, examiner may convert them by examiner's amendment or set a ONE MONTH time limit for appellant to rewrite dependent claims in independent form; extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) will not be permitted in that one-month case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph ¶12.292 (At Least One Allowed Claim) provides the one-month time and warns that failure to comply will result in cancellation of the dependent claims and issuance of the application with the allowed claims only. Ensure proper bracketed claim numbers are filled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure where Board affirms but also enters 37 CFR 41.50(b) rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board affirms an examiner’s rejection but also enters a new ground under 41.50(b), subsequent procedure depends on appellant action: (A) if appellant elects to proceed before the examiner by amending or submitting new evidence, the Board’s affirmance will be treated as nonfinal; (B) if appellant merely presents arguments without amendment/evidence, jurisdiction should remain with the Board and such arguments should be treated as requests for rehearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only when appellant amends or submits new evidence must prosecution be reopened and the case returned to the examiner. If an examiner receives a reply containing only arguments against the new ground, the appeal should be returned to the Board for handling. Prosecution before examiner of 41.50(b) rejection may incidentally overcome the affirmed rejection, possibly leading to allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of inaction on 37 CFR 41.50(b) rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board makes a new rejection under 37 CFR 41.50(b) and appellant takes no action within two months, the proceedings as to the rejected claims are considered terminated and examiner should proceed per MPEP guidance (e.g., issue form paragraph ¶12.297 indicating period for seeking court review has lapsed and identifying formal matters to correct).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should set shortened statutory periods for correction of formal matters (TWO MONTHS in sample ¶12.297) to avoid abandonment; identify allowed claims and outstanding formal matters in communications.
